baseline.coverage: All current runtime/core/gateway/shared source and tests/core/gateway/runtime content plus tests/fixtures/native-env.ts exactly match the complete full7 semantic baseline and its prior complete-review chain. No added, omitted or removed assigned file.

method: Complete scoped incremental audit: compared the actual SHA256 of all 205 assigned files against both frozen full7/full8 manifests, checked the exact path set, and recomputed the canonical whole-source snapshot at the start and end. Inherit the prior complete semantic review explicitly; no claim that all unchanged bodies were freshly reread. Reread the current backend preview/media/read-versus-mutation consumers listed below to evaluate this UI lifecycle-only delta. Do not independently accept the four changed WEB files here: their review is assigned to the runtime agent. No tests or live operations were executed during this audit.

currentConsumerReview.focus: Attachment history/media and workspace status/diff/refs/download remain reads; Git commit remains a project-scoped configuration mutation. UI preview cancellation cannot enter a mutation by changing read admission.

currentConsumerReview.depth: read dispatch and mutation admission/maintenance/beforeWrite branches
currentConsumerReview.focus: Reads require the current connection and resolve registered project parameters. A commit still requires its explicit durable operation identity, reservation, owner/authorization checks and maintenance/idle gates; no preview result or abort implicitly dispatches it.

currentConsumerReview.depth: HTTP response/backend lifetime and authenticated RPC branches
currentConsumerReview.focus: Request admission remains charged until backend and response settle. A browser fetch cancellation can close its response but does not declare submitted backend work cancelled or reset durable outcome. Origin, session, CSRF and admission-time WS lease remain checked; post-dispatch response failure remains unknown.

Read helper dispatch remains separated from durable writes. Git commit still runs through configure and witness reservation/acknowledgement. Cancellation of browser status/diff reads neither clears a witness nor alters history or active process ownership.

currentConsumerReview.depth: download/diff/commit request validation and helper execution bounds
currentConsumerReview.focus: Explicit head, head revision, index revision, author and message remain required for commits; file download requires an exact revision. Read and write helper budgets/timeouts and command construction are unchanged.

Positive write acknowledgement remains durable and identity-bound before public completion; unknown delivery cannot be downgraded by UI cleanup. Witness acknowledgement requires matching request/result identities and keeps proof on failed helper cleanup.
A commit still requires valid new/previous object IDs, index revision and recovery operation ID. Local confirmation lifecycle does not replace this receipt contract.

currentConsumerReview.depth: workspace routing and attachment/history/read, thread/media/read dispatch cases
currentConsumerReview.focus: UI cancellation changes only its local observation lifetime; method routing still selects retained attachments or generated-media readers, with no conversion/resume/model-provider mutation introduced.

History media remains an exact retained path belonging to the given thread, live state required. A project change in the viewer does not grant arbitrary native paths or release thread attachment references.

Media ID, thread/turn/item identity, first-chunk native membership validation, history revision, closed-state recheck, bounded chunks and cache eviction remain intact. Browser aborting a chunk does not transfer its capability to another thread or overwrite native history.

impactConclusion: The new source changes affect when client preview lifecycle cleanup finishes and add regressions, plus a maintainer lesson. All 205 server/shared/associated test files are byte-identical to the complete reviewed baseline. Completing a local read before rendering its confirmation does not bypass actual commit validation, change operation identity or authorize replay. Releasing obsolete browser media resources does not alter retained attachment ownership, native generation history, media chunk identity, cache budgets, provider lock, shared account configuration or process lifecycle. The WEB reviewer must separately establish that the client lifecycle change is correct.
limitations: This scope retains prior complete content/semantic review with actual current byte verification; hashing alone is not represented as a newly performed complete semantic read.
